question: persister
constraint: using only data that are already publicly available (no new experiments)
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out using only data that are already publicly available (no new experiments). Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Pre-existing vs. induced state from lineage-barcoding datasets
ideas.description: Reanalyze public clonal barcoding scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Cellular Barcoding studies of BRAF-inhibitor-treated melanoma, EGFR-inhibitor-treated lung cancer, Shaffer/Hata/Oren/Goyal data in GEO). Test whether sister cells' pre-treatment transcriptomes predict survival, and quantify how much of survival is heritable versus stochastic, to separate pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment signature of persisters
ideas.description: Use public paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell expression data to build a classifier of the rare pre-treatment cell state, such as the NGFR-high, AXL-high or dedifferentiated melanoma states, and the EMT-like or drug-tolerant states. Validate it on held-out cell lines and on public drug-response data (GDSC, CTRP, DepMap PRISM) by testing whether the signature predicts tolerance across lines.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility and epigenetic memory meta-analysis
ideas.description: Integrate public scATAC-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq and histone-mark data (H3K27me3, KDM5 targets, SWI/SNF) from persisters and parental cells. Find the transcription factor motifs and enhancers that open or close in persisters, and check whether those accessibility changes are already present in a subset of untreated cells, to identify the regulators that carry the memory.

ideas.title: Transcriptional-noise and cell-cycle/metabolic state modeling
ideas.description: Using public time-course scRNA-seq and live-cell imaging datasets, calculate gene-expression variability, cell-cycle phase (slow-cycling or G0/G1 arrest) and metabolic signatures (oxidative phosphorylation, ferroptosis defense via GPX4). Fit stochastic state-switching models to estimate the switching rates and ask whether survival is better explained by noise, quiescence or metabolic state.

ideas.title: Genetic-ruling-out and clinical concordance analysis
ideas.description: Reanalyze public whole-exome and whole-genome data and copy-number profiles from persister cells, resistant clones and matched patient biopsies (such as minimal residual disease samples). Rule out pre-existing mutations and copy-number changes as the cause, and check whether the persister transcriptional programs also appear in patient on-treatment samples and associate with relapse in TCGA and clinical trial cohorts.
